<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/core.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via executionContext (literal, a string literal in platformSystemApi))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via executionContext (literal, a string literal in platformSystemApi))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via executionContext (literal, a string literal in platformSystemApi))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via executionContext (literal, a string literal in platformSystemApi))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/core.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **64** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f5d1753f05860d20bb017c74a78e068e6916e6ad` — the merge of head `04704e057f1cfa1a34d753b0a9178a259d13988b` into base `6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f5d1753f05860d20bb017c74a78e068e6916e6ad && git checkout f5d1753f05860d20bb017c74a78e068e6916e6ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45 04704e057f1cfa1a34d753b0a9178a259d13988b && git checkout -B drift-repro 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45 && git merge --no-ff 04704e057f1cfa1a34d753b0a9178a259d13988b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6f2bd4f84c98dcac81b0d745fcc16a35641ecc45` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### L1 review (#35052) · 2026-11-18T05:46Z

L1: REWORK (one must-fix, in the changeset only)
Head-sha: 030dc834ba3b375fde0b6747aad478d9534aca4c

This is the first L1 on this PR. I read the full diff against the merge-base `0e46840fca`: 13 files, +365/−19. I also read the card, the claim 6968536278, the claim amendment 6970237640 and the os-dev report 6970196156.

**The fix, read against the claim's corrected premise.**
- `persistAuditTrailRow` now writes `sys_audit_log` and `sys_activity` through `platformSystemApi(api) ?? api.sudo()`. That is the one-line change the card's goal needs, and the only runtime change in plugin-audit.
- `ScopedContextFacet.platformSystemApi` builds `{ ...executionContext, isSystem: true }`, removes the mark with `withoutAppAutomationElevation`, drops `flowRunId`, and derives through `derive`. Every other key is kept (transaction, tenant, user, permissions), and the objectql pin asserts that, `transaction` identity included. `derive` carries `appAuthored`, so the permanent-delete refusal on an app-authored api is kept.
- `sudo()` is unchanged. The CONTROL pins (objectql: `sudo()` keeps the mark and the run; plugin-security: an action body's own `sudo()` insert into `sys_activity` still logs the deprecation) hold the `app-automation-elevation.ts` header rule that a body's own elevation stays marked.
- `withoutAppAutomationElevation` returns the same object when no mark is present and a fresh copy otherwise. Its pin checks both, plus `null`.
- The plugin-security change is docblocks only. The predicate `isSystem AND (flowRunId OR mark)` is not edited and no object is exempted, so ruling 6787890900 and ADR-0073 ruling 6354966423 are untouched.

**Shape and scope.**
- `Fixes #35052` is on the first card line, with no closing keyword next to another open card. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the diff: two new exports, no accept set widened, no `packages/spec` change.
- The objectql paths are outside the original claim, which said "stop on breach". Amendment 6970237640 widens the surface to these 13 paths with the measured reason (the writer holds only the hook's `ScopedContext`, whose context is private) and records the seat's answers A/A to the report's two questions. I accept the amended surface. The flow-run half (Q2) sits on the same line and the same describe, so it stays.
- No `content/docs/releases/` change, no unrelated file. `check-governed-merges --pr 35124`: not governed (0 of 13 paths), 384 changed lines, under the 3,000-line threshold.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` owes the `TIER_DEFAULT` declaration-face contract record, which your area runs after this L1. No narrowing and no governed text, so no CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER face is owed.

**Changeset.** `.changeset/35052-platform-audit-write-unmarked.md` is new and edits no changeset on main, so it does not affect the 18.6.0 freeze or Version PR #33849. It bumps `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `objectql` and `core` as `patch`, which covers every published package with a runtime change (plugin-security has docblocks only). Apart from M1, I checked its sentences against the diff:
- "It wrote both through the `sudo()` of the hook api it is handed, and `sudo()` spreads the audited write's context." This matches `persistAuditTrailRow` and the facet's `sudo`.
- "an action body's or a system hook's app-automation elevation mark, or a flow run's `flowRunId`". These are the three provenance sources the pins cover (action, hook, system flow, user flow).
- "Today that logged the … warning on the first such write." This matches the report's measurement and the claim's premise (warn only, no refusal arm yet).
- "minus the app-automation mark and minus `flowRunId`. Every other key is kept" matches the facet and the objectql pin.
- "What an automation writes itself is unchanged … `sudo()` itself is unchanged too" matches the CONTROL pins and the untouched `sudo` body.

**Tests and evidence.**
- plugin-security: a real-stack describe (`ObjectKernel`, `ObjectQLPlugin` over better-sqlite3, the real `AuditPlugin` and `SecurityPlugin`). For each of the four contexts, it asserts no deprecation line and exactly one `sys_audit_log` and one `sys_activity` row read back. Plus the CONTROL.
- objectql: the derivation pin, the `sudo()` CONTROL, the not-engine-built case, and the published-face symbol count moving from 3 to 4, with `PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API` asserted absent from the entry.
- core: the `withoutAppAutomationElevation` pin.
- Ablation: reverting the writer line to `api.sudo()` turned the 4 cases red, each with both Deprecated lines, while the CONTROL stayed green. The restore was verified (blob == HEAD). The facet's two strips are held by the objectql pin rather than by a separate ablation, which I accept.
- `dispatch-gates --commands`: 79 derived, 79 run, all exit 0, including `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` re-read at the final head.

**CI at this head**, read from check-runs (68) at review time: 18 success, 13 skipped, 37 in progress, none failed. The M1 fix moves the head, so I will read the check-runs at the new head with the delta.

#### Must-fix
- **M1. The changeset still declares `Clause-②: no`.** The PR body and amendment 6970237640 say `yes (widening)`, and the diff adds two published names. The changeset line is not only a record: `scripts/release-github-releases.mjs` sorts a release bullet by its `Clause-②:` arm. A non-protocol `Clause-②: yes` goes under 新增能力 (added), and `Clause-②: no` with `Metadata-protocol: none` goes under the other fixes. As written, the two new exports would be listed as a plain fix. Change the line to `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. I'll read that delta alone, plus CI at the new head.

#### Should-fix
- **S1. Enforce the platform's own system api's ⛔ line in code, not only in the docblock.** `platformSystemApi` is now a published export, and its docblock says "⛔ Never for a write the automation itself asked for". Today the derivation sheds the provenance on any engine-built api, including an app-authored hook's api. `sudo()` on that same api adds the `'hook'` mark. Suggested rule: on an app-authored api, the platform's own system api keeps that api's provenance, as `sudo()` does. Pin it with one case next to the CONTROL. The audit writer is registered in code, so its api is never app-authored and the fix is unaffected. If you decline, say why in the declaration-face record, since that is where the published name is judged.

#### Notes
- **N1.** The PR body says the key "follows the `SEED_USER_GRANTS` pattern", but `SEED_USER_GRANTS` is a module-local `Symbol()` and this key is `Symbol.for(...)`. The stated reason (a reader loaded from the other entry or build) is the one `APP_AUTOMATION_ELEVATION` gives, and I accept it. With a registry key, "no name on the published face" holds for the type face only. The declaration-face record should read it that way.
- **N2.** The card's Done-when asks for a pin "with the refusal enabled". That arm has not shipped, so the pins assert no deprecation and the rows landing instead, as the claim's corrected premise says. When the refusal arm ships, its PR should run this describe with the arm on.
- **N3.** The `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` test imports in plugin-security are existing devDependencies. No `package.json` or lockfile changed.
- **Landing.** The 18.6.0 freeze holds this PR. Owed next: M1 and its delta L1, then the declaration-face contract record (your area).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `04704e057f1cfa1a34d753b0a9178a259d13988b`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). There is no `packages/spec` path and no governed path among the 13 files. Inputs read: card #35052 (body, claim 6968536278, regrade 6969792923, os-dev reports 6970196156 and 6972225261, amendment 6970237640), PR #35124 (body, file list, docs-drift 6970205429, L1 REWORK 6970299173 with N1–N3, L1 delta ACCEPT 6972295206), the net diff against merge-base `0e46840fca`, and the 72 check-runs on the head: 59 success, 13 skipped, none failed, cancelled or in progress. Code outside the diff was read but not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface the diff adds.** There are exactly two new published names, and no accept set is widened. No schema, request shape, metadata key or wire route changes.

- **`platformSystemApi(api)`** is new on `@objectstack/objectql` `.` (`index.ts:387`) and `./core` (`core.ts:73`).
  - It returns `undefined` for an api the engine did not build. Otherwise it returns the result of the symbol-keyed member `ScopedContext#[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]`.
  - **Right.** The only consumer is `@objectstack/objectql/core`, imported by plugin-audit's `persistAuditTrailRow`. The `.` copy has no in-repo consumer, but it follows the lean-entry-mirrors-barrel convention that `core.ts` states, the same one `ScopedContext` already follows.
  - **Necessary.** The writer holds only the hook's `ScopedContext`, and that class's `executionContext` is private. A published reader is the only supported way to reach it. If plugin-audit spelled the registry key itself, that would be the same reach with no contract.
- **`withoutAppAutomationElevation(context)`** is new on `@objectstack/core` (`security/index.ts:623`).
  - **Necessary.** objectql (`engine-scoped-context.ts`) takes the mark off across a package boundary, and the mark's key handling lives in core beside `markAppAutomationElevation` and `carryAppAutomationElevation`.
  - The behaviour matches the docblock: the same object when there is no mark, a fresh copy otherwise, and `null` or primitives handed back unchanged. It is pinned in `app-automation-elevation.test.ts`.
  - Its ⛔ ("never for a write the automation itself makes") is a usage rule on a pure function and cannot be enforced in code. It also adds no reach: the key is `Symbol.for(...)`, so any in-process caller could already strip it with object rest or `delete`.
- **`ScopedContext` gains a fourth symbol-keyed prototype member.** The key is not exported from either entry, and the published-face pin in `hook-run-as.test.ts` moves from 3 to 4 and asserts `PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API` is absent. **Right.**

**What the derivation does.** It sheds two things and keeps everything else.

- **Read in code:** `ScopedContextFacet.platformSystemApi` builds `{ ...executionContext, isSystem: true }`, removes the mark, drops `flowRunId`, and builds the child with `derive`. Every other key is kept, including `transaction` (by identity), `tenantId`, `userId`, `permissions`, `attributedUserId`, `performedBy` and the skip flags. The objectql pin asserts this.
- **`flowRunId` dropped.** The ledger row's own insert no longer reports `provenance.flowRunId` to the hooks that fire on that insert. The ledger content is unaffected, because `auditRow` and `activityRow` are built beforehand from the audited write's context. I found no hook on `sys_audit_log` or `sys_activity` that reads it. The approvals lock reads `provenance.flowRunId` only for records with a pending request.
- **Mark shed.** The `'action'` mark is also read by the owner stamp (`isActionBodyElevation`, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:687`). That stamp applies only when the object has `owner_id`. Both ledger objects are `managedBy: 'append-only'`, and the registry gives managed tables no owner anchor. So nothing about row ownership changes. **Neutral, right.**

**The S1 guard, read as part of the published name's contract (as L1 asked).** On an app-authored api, `platformSystemApi` returns what `sudo()` returns: the mark and `flowRunId` are kept.

- `ScopedContextFacet.platformSystemApi` opens with `if (this.appAuthored) return ScopedContextFacet.sudo.call(this);`.
- `appAuthored` is set only by `appAuthoredHookApi`, which `installRunAsApi` installs for every hook the hook binder binds. `derive` copies it to every child: `sudo`, `withRunAs`, `[SEED_USER_GRANTS]`, `transaction` (`engine-scoped-context.ts:221`, `:247`), `beginTransaction`, and `[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]` itself.
- So an app-authored hook's in-process `handler`, under any `runAs`, gets nothing from `platformSystemApi` that its own `sudo()` does not already give it.
- **Pinned:** the OPERATOR, ACTION and RUN contexts under `runAs: 'inherit'`, each checked against a `sudo()` control. The pin was red-first at `1e2cc57e35` and red again with the guard line ablated (report 6972225261).
- The `withRunAs('system')` and `'user'` children are covered by `derive` in code, not by a separate pin. I accept that.
- The audit writer's api comes from `buildHookApi`, which builds a fresh, non-app-authored `ScopedContext` from the write's context. So the guard does not undo the fix. The plugin-security real-stack describe passes 160/160 at this head's code.

**Can an app author or an app-authored hook reach it to shed provenance?**

- **A sandboxed body (hook, action or job; QuickJS): no.** The VM's `ctx.api` is a fixed allowlist: `object(name)` with the READ and WRITE leaves, and `transaction`. It has no `sudo` and no symbol member, and the VM has its own symbol registry. No host object crosses into it.
- **An app-authored hook's in-process `handler`: it can reach the function and the key, but sheds nothing (S1).** Spelling `Symbol.for('objectstack.objectql.platformSystemApi')` and calling the member directly runs the same facet body, so the key gives no route around the guard. **N1, read as asked:** "no name on the published face" holds for the type face only. The registry key is reachable at runtime by anyone who spells it, and that is safe only because the guard sits in the member body, not in the reader. This is right as built.
- **An app author's host code action handler: yes.** This is the published-route gap. See F1.

**F1 · should-fix: the guarded line stops at app-authored hook apis, and the published contract does not say what happens on the action door's api.**

- **The api.** A code package registers in-process action handlers through `engine.registerAction`. This is the documented pattern: `examples/app-todo` registers from `onEnable(ctx.ql)`. Each handler receives `buildActionApi`'s `ctx.api` (runtime `action-execution.ts`). That api is `ql.createContext(...)` with the `'action'` mark, and it is not app-authored.
- **What the docs promise about it.** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` rows 1b and 2 say the mark is set on "every handler an action door dispatches (a host code action handler included)". Row 1b says that context is refused identity-assignment writes.
- **What happens on that api.** `platformSystemApi(ctx.api)` returns a system api with neither the mark nor the run. Its writes to `sys_member`, `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set` or `sys_invitation`, and its inserts into append-only objects, then pass as platform writes.
- **It also leaves the runtime seams behind.** Runtime's `deriveThroughSeam` (`stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts`) says it is "one definition of what a scoped API can derive, so neither layer can leave a route around it". Its `default` arm binds the symbol member to the unwrapped target, so the derived api comes back outside the stored-metadata read seam (#21454) and the landed-write answer (#28861) that wrap that `ctx.api`.
- **Not a code defect today.**
  - It gives that caller no new reach: the handler's package registers through `ql` and can already `ql.createContext({ isSystem: true })`, and TypeScript `private engine` is not a runtime boundary.
  - The engine cannot tell this api from the platform hook api the audit writer holds, because both are non-app-authored and carry the inherited `'action'` mark. So a guard like S1 would need an action-api flag and is out of this card's surface.
- **But the contract is incomplete.** The published name's contract (`platform-system-api.ts` header, the `ScopedContext#[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]` docblock, the changeset) describes the enforced line as "the one api it knows is the automation's" and names no other.
- **Fix, in surface.** Add one paragraph to `platform-system-api.ts` that:
  - names the host code action handler's `ctx.api` as an automation api the engine does not guard, and why: it is indistinguishable from the platform hook api, and the handler already holds the engine;
  - states that a seam-wrapped api's `deriveThroughSeam` walk does not cover this member.
- **Optional follow-up card, outside this surface.** Add the key to `deriveThroughSeam`'s walk, or give the action door's api a provenance flag the facet can guard on.
- **Graded should-fix, not nit,** because it is the published name's own contract text, the thing this record judges. A delta read is owed.

**F2 · nit: `withoutAppAutomationElevation`'s docblock says "a fresh copy with every other own property".** Object rest copies own enumerable properties only, and it reads accessors into data properties. There is no effect today, because the one in-repo caller passes a fresh spread. It should read "every other own enumerable property".

**Docblock corrections in the diff, checked against the code.**

- `engine.ts` `sudo()` now says it adds no mark but keeps one the context already carries: true of `ScopedContextFacet.sudo`.
- The two `flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts` docblocks were changed from "carries no mark" to "adds none, keeps a carried one; the ledger rows are the exception": true.
- The `app-automation-elevation.ts` header gains a "Where it is taken off" section. That is true, and it leaves the "⛔ never on `sudo()`" rule intact.
- The predicate `isSystem AND (flowRunId OR mark)` is not edited, no object is exempted, and rulings 6787890900 and ADR-0073 6354966423 are untouched.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset.** `.changeset/35052-platform-audit-write-unmarked.md` bumps `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/core` at `patch`.
